text: Databases are essential for storing and organizing data. The two main types are SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases use tables with fixed rows and columns, making them great for structured data and complex queries. NoSQL databases are more flexible, handling unstructured data like documents or graphs. Data modeling is the process of designing how data is structured, whether in tables or other formats. To find specific information, you write queries—instructions that retrieve or manipulate data. Indexes are special structures that speed up queries by allowing the database to locate data faster. Understanding these concepts helps you choose the right database for your needs.
